# gr-rds

**Decodes the data carried alongside broadcast FM — station names, traffic**

- **Version recorded:** 3.10
- **Categories:** `listening`, `sdr`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/bastibl/gr-rds>
- **Needs first:** `gnuradio`

## What it does

Decodes RDS, the low-rate data channel on a 57 kHz subcarrier of a broadcast FM signal: station name, programme type, radio text, alternative frequencies, the clock, and TMC traffic messages. It also transmits it, which is where the module's name ends in "transceiver".

## Why you would want it

It is the friendliest possible introduction to real demodulation. The signal is strong, always present, and the result is human-readable text that either matches what the station is called or does not -- immediate feedback that no weak-signal work gives you. As a first GNU Radio flow graph to understand rather than merely run, it is hard to beat.

## Before it will work

Any SDR that covers the FM broadcast band and a couple of hundred kHz of bandwidth. A wire will do for an antenna.

## How it installs

- apt: `gr-rds`

## Known problems

RDS needs a solid signal: a station you can hear through noise will produce partial or garbled text, which looks like a decoder bug and is not. The transmit side is real RF on a broadcast band and is not lawful to radiate in most places -- the module will happily generate it into a dummy load or a file, and what leaves an antenna is your responsibility.
